items.title: Concerns raised over AusAlert emergency warning system
items.description: The rollout of a national emergency warning system is in doubt as most state and territory governments say they will keep their state-based systems.

items.title: Live: Penny Wong raises missile test with Chinese foreign minister
items.description: Penny Wong has raised China's missile test and detention of Australian democracy activist Dr Yang Hengjun with the Chinese foreign minister. Follow live.

items.title: Albanese's career mirrors Howard's in two important ways
items.description: Anthony Albanese has been in near-fatal vehicle accidents not once, but three times. Politically, his is also a story of survival against the odds.

items.title: Woman's family wrongly told she was dead in hospital identity error
items.description: A Melbourne hospital apologises after mixing up the medical data of two people, resulting in one of them being wrongly declared dead by police.

items.title: Boy charged with murdering mother, attempting to kill sister in Perth
items.description: A 16-year-old boy is charged with murdering his mother and attempting to kill his sister in an alleged domestic violence homicide in suburban Perth.

items.title: Family's cross-contamination nightmare after contractors spread mould
items.description: A Queensland family is living in an overcrowded caravan and shed after insurance provider Suncorp exacerbated damage in their home, initially caused by a leak.

items.title: NT enacts 'significant overhaul' of child protection system
items.description: The Northern Territory parliament has passed legislative changes to the child protection system, with the Country Liberal Party (CLP) describing its new laws as "the most significant overhaul of the Territory's child protection system in a generation".

items.title: 'We do not want to highlight this yet': AI data centre's FAQ slip-up
items.description: Data centre builder Firmus posted a statement, since removed, indicating its intention to get some of its cooling water from the state-owned irrigation system, adding "but we do not want to highlight this yet".

items.title: Map reveals Australia's 'pharmacy deserts' are not all in the bush
items.description: Australia's "pharmacy deserts" have been mapped for the first time, revealing remote NT communities and outer-city Melbourne have fewer pharmacies per person than some other parts of the country.

items.title: Gas tax, gambling and AI at stake at the Labor conference
items.description: Labor members and unions are gearing up for fights over gambling, gas and AI at the party's national conference later this week.

items.title: How school is different for Jewish Australian kids
items.description: The Royal Commission into Antisemitism and Social Cohesion hears from Jewish school leaders about how they need to implement extraordinary and expensive security measures.

items.title: Hegseth outlines cost of Iran war at Senate hearing
items.description: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is being questioned on the cost of the war against Iran, his idea of testosterone screening for troops, and the number of service people who have died.

items.title: Zelenskyy names new Ukrainian commander-in-chief
items.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy replaces the country's commander-in-chief after protests against his sacking of the defence minister last week.

items.title: Spanish chief accuses FIFA boss of 'destroying the football industry'
items.description: FIFA president Gianni Infantino comes in for more heavy criticism, this time at the hands of La Liga boss Javier Tebas.

items.title: New Ozploitation horror is like Puberty Blues from hell
items.description: After spending years in special effects and make-up, filmmaker Mia'Kate Russell's ocker nightmare Penny Lane Is Dead has made it to the silver screen.

items.title: Travel quiz: join us for a trip around the world
items.description: Where are macadamia nuts indigenous to? And what’s the capital city of Switzerland?

items.title: Stingers hitting new heights thanks to shared love for each other
items.description: Australia's women's water polo team, the Stingers, were the most successful Australian team at the Paris Olympics, winning a stunning silver medal. This is the secret to their success.

items.title: Cameron McEvoy has lived a life between trips to Glasgow
items.description: As one of just two Australian swimmers returning to Glasgow for a second Commonwealth Games, Cameron McEvoy is taking time to appreciate how much has happened to him in the past 12 years.

items.title: AI companies 'stole' Australian culture, news bosses say, as they call for licensing deals
items.description: The heads of the ABC, SBS, Nine and News Corp say AI companies should strike licensing deals rather than freely train on Australian news, warning journalism is a public good that must be protected.

items.title: Live: ASX to rise as oil prices hit five-week high, Wall Street tech stocks rebound
items.description: The Australian share market is likely to start its day higher after Wall Street's beaten-down tech and semiconductor stocks rebounded sharply overnight. Oil prices surged to a five-week high as Donald Trump signalled the US is "not finished" attacking Iran. Follow live.

items.title: Judgment day for Rebel Wilson's messy defamation case
items.description: Hollywood star Rebel Wilson will learn today whether she defamed the lead actor on her "fun girl-power" film, in a judgment to be handed down in the Federal Court.

items.title: Repatriation effort for homeless man found dead outside Sydney station
items.description: The mother of a homeless man whose death outside a Sydney train station went unnoticed for days is pleading for her son's remains to be returned to Nepal.

items.title: WA man dies after not being able to get antipsychotic medication
items.description: Bradley Buswell, aged in his 40s and living with schizophrenia, died in state care after his medication became unavailable due to national shortages. An ongoing coronial inquest is probing the circumstances of his death.

items.title: Victorian teachers are going on strike again — here's what you need to know
items.description: Victorian state school teachers and educators are going ahead with their second 24-hour strike this year after union members rejected the government's latest pay offer.

items.title: Players and fans made the World Cup a success, but the politics shouldn't be forgotten
items.description: The biggest ever World Cup brought diverse communities together and galvanised its non-traditional footballing co-hosts, but the concerns raised from the start have not disappeared in the positive afterglow.
